title: Roadblock detection fix: where the live tests stand

short.lead: Superseded: the live tests have since run and four of five cases behave correctly (see the QA page for pull request 602). At the time of writing, main was merged into the branch and pushed, but the five live test sessions could not run because the 5-hour usage limit was reached until 9:20pm.
items: Live sessions blocked by the usage limit
Running claude -p (Claude Code's non-interactive mode) with a plain prompt returned the 5-hour limit message. So all five sessions in live_roadblocks.py exited with code 1 before any hook ran.
Done later: the rerun after switching the CLI login is recorded on the QA page.

items: The one live PASS proves nothing
The three-methods case passed only because it expected zero blocks, and no session ran at all, so zero blocks were seen.
Ignore that result. The later rerun is the real evidence.
verify_tools.py fails check A16 on this machine
Check A16 tries to uninstall house-rules@aj-house-rules, which is not installed on this machine. The merge did not cause the failure.
Run verify_tools.py on a machine that has the plugin installed, or leave this as a known failure on this machine.

changes: Main merged into the branch and pushed (accdfae9)
verify.py shows 8 of 994 checks failing. These are the same 8 Windows failures as before the merge.
The next session can pick up from the 9:20pm rerun.
